We don't need a handful of people doing zero waste perfectly. We need millions of people doing it imperfectly.
-Anne-Marie Bonneau of ZeroWasteChef

New GreenSpot Coordinator

We are thrilled to introduce Christy Walters as our new GreenSpot Coordinator! Christy brings years of experience with outreach to residents and businesses as it pertains to sustainability and the energy to match. She is the newest addition to the Sustainable Columbus team. Dave Celebrezze (previous coordinator) will focus his efforts as the Resilience and Behavior Change Manager within Sustainable Columbus.

"Through business endeavors and my personal life, I have always aspired to lead by example and encourage others on their sustainability journey. Progress not perfection is my mantra, and I believe in showing up every day for people and the planet.

With a career that spans events, non-profits, board work (both participating on and collaborating with boards), community outreach, and eco-education, I believe this is my perfect dream job, and I am so thankful for this opportunity! Thank you so much, I look forward to working with all of you." -Christy Walters

GreenSpot Community Backyards rebates-for businesses

New to the GreenSpot Community Backyards program this year, City of Columbus businesses and organizations can apply for up to a $2,500 reimbursement on green infrastructure projects, such as rain gardens, native plantings, tree planting, or rainwater collection.

The rebate can be used toward supplies, native plants, mulch, rainwater collection systems, rain barrels, soil amendments, and educational signage. Projects must be located within the City of Columbus. Funds are limited and available on a first-come, first-served basis. Special consideration will be given to projects benefitting underserved populations and projects located in designated Columbus CelebrateOne neighborhoods, opportunity zones, and areas with less than 20% tree canopy cover. Participating businesses will also be signed up as a Columbus GreenSpot member. To learn more and apply, click here.

Smart Columbus Acceleration Partner Program

Smart Columbus, a team of the Columbus Partnership, has gathered 35+ leading employers under the Acceleration Partner Program (APP). The APP is a powerful network of organizations who are committed to achieving a more sustainable and prosperous Columbus Region by pursuing goals aligned with three key pillars: Transportation, Energy & Buildings, and Digitalization.

Smart Columbus facilitates programming for Sustainability, ESG, and IT professionals, provides educational resources and expert vendors, and manages initiatives to support Acceleration Partners’ ESG priorities.

To learn more about the Acceleration Partner Program, or explore how your organization can participate in additional Smart Columbus programming, please email Marcus Carano.

Follow Smart Columbus on social media to see upcoming events.

GreenSpot and ESG

What is ESG and why does it matter to Columbus?

ESG stands for Environmental, Social, and Governance.  Instead of a business answering only to their investors/profitability, they are demonstrating responsibility and social credibility to the wider demographic of stakeholders, employees, customers, regulators, community, while taking future generations into account. 

GreenSpot aims to learn/share the benefits of ESG for both sustainability and social reasons considering the term to be a subject that encourages the message of Social Responsibility and not a position. 

As the world shifts towards social responsibility, ESG practices can also provide an organization with a competitive advantage with recruiting and retaining talent, optimizing operational efficiency and increasing resiliency through sustainable business practices, public relations, and increasing marketing opportunities while being proactive to the global changes.

In the heart of it all, as Columbus becomes more populated with more business ventures, a collaborative investment in ESG principles from corporations, non-profits, and academic institutions can lead to outsized impact and meaningful results aligned with the City of Columbus’s goal of carbon neutrality by 2050.

As the GreenSpot ESG working group, we aim to support a broader form of transparency, accountability, and ensure better information from companies while starting to understand and share what we know as a Social Responsibility and not a position.

In the near future we will have more information about ESG on the GreenSpot website and will host a virtual meeting covering ESG 101. If you organization has adopted an ESG strategy and is looking for more engagement, please see Smart Columbus’s Sustainability Leaders Group, which gathers senior Sustainability and ESG professionals from leading employers to share best practices and identify areas for collaboration. For more information and to learn how to become involved, contact Marcus Carano.

Also covered will be the various websites that deliver recycling education making it easier for you and your business to get your team to Recycle Right. Sign up here.

GreenSpot tip o' the day

GreenSpot resources

GreenSpot has many resources available to your organization to conserve and protect water, conserve energy, reduce waste, and green your transportation. On the website, you’ll find our guide on the Case for a Sustainability Manager, How to Start a Green Team at Work guide, and links to resources provided by partners such as SWACO, MORPC, EPA, Columbia Gas of Ohio, and more. If you have any questions or are stuck in a rut in your sustainability journey, email us! GreenSpot@columbus.gov.

Become a Water Quality Partner

Calling all Franklin County businesses and employees! Join the Water Quality Partnership to learn how your business can prevent stormwater pollution and improve water quality in our local streams and rivers. Join over 200 local businesses who have pledged to simple practices that keep Franklin County’s streams and rivers clean – practices that you might even be doing already. After you take the pledge, your business will receive a certificate of participation, access to continuing education on how you can help water quality, public recognition on our website and social media, and a window cling to show partners and customers and your local municipality that you care about water quality. Learn more and take the pledge today.

Columbus Commitment: Achieving Pay Equity pledge

Did you know that overall, women in the United States are paid 83 cents for every dollar paid to white men for the same job? For women of color, the inequity is even greater. For example, Latina women earn only 55 cents for every dollar earned by a white man.

Pay inequality isn’t just a women’s issue, it’s a family issue and an economic issue. These lost wages mean women and their families have less money to support themselves, save and invest for the future as well as spend on goods and services.

The Columbus Women’s Commission launched the next phase of the Columbus Commitment to close the gender and race-based wage gap in Columbus.

The campaign, 100 Adopters. 100 Days. 100% Committed, runs through July 3rd, and aims to add 100 new Pay Equity Pledge adopters. The Commission would love to add your organization to the list as one of our 100 new adopters!

Right now 38% of GreenSpot business members have taken the pledge. Visit the Commission’s website for more information on the Columbus Commitment. Have Questions? Reach out to Christina Ratleff to learn more about the pledge.

Heat Map volunteers needed

Columbus and Franklin County are seeking volunteers to help collect environmental data about the hottest and coolest places in our region during an upcoming heat wave this summer. Data collected by volunteers during the joint one-day heat mapping campaign will be used to develop temperature and heat index maps for Columbus and parts of Franklin County. Additionally it will help address heat-related vulnerabilities across the region. [Participating volunteers will be granted a stipend of $$ for completion of their responsibilities.]

In short, volunteers will drive along a predetermined route over three separate one-hour periods during a hot day collecting data from equipment that will be provided. We need three people per route—a driver, navigator, and backup.
Drivers will need a valid driver’s license, auto insurance, and access to a vehicle. In addition to the three hours of data collection, volunteers will first be asked to attend a one-hour Volunteer Training Session, complete a short knowledge quiz, and sign a liability waiver.

The date of the heat mapping will be sometime between August 5th and 17th. We will know a few days before the mapping will occur and will notify volunteers.

If your employees are interested in participating in this opportunity, or would like to learn more, please respond to this Volunteer Intake Form  or email David R. Celebrezze.

EMPOWERED! Young adult jobs program

Launched by Mayor Ginther, the goal of EMPOWERED! is to provide pathways to good paying careers that lead to upward mobility in the construction and clean energy sector for Columbus youth ages 18-24. If you know anyone that may be interested (example: employee’s son or daughter) contact Katie Delvin at IMPACT or potential participants can use the QR code to fill out an interest form.

How to be sustainable around the 4th of July

With 4th of July right around the corner, it’s important to remember our commitment to sustainability. If you’re hosting a corporate party or firework viewing at your workplace, here are some tips to keep it green. Ditch the disposable plates and utensils and provide plastic reusable ones, instead. If you don’t have enough, advertise the event as BYOPlate! We know this makes a few dishes, but did Ben Franklin have a dishwasher? (No, they barely had electricity!) If you’re grilling, buy your meat in reusable containers from a butcher rather than the cling wrapped beef on Styrofoam (or go the fake meat route!), and reduce your emissions by opting for propane instead of charcoal. Refreshments are important in this recent heat wave, so help your employees cool down with large water coolers for refilling reusable water bottles instead of bottled water. Some waste is unavoidable, so make recycling easy by providing large clearly-marked bins for plastic, paper, and metal recyclables. Finally, consider a keg instead of cases of individual drinks. Cheers to a sustainable 4th of July!

Did you know they were a GreenSpot? DLZ

Sustainability has become an integral part of the DLZ culture. Since the pandemic, DLZ has tremendously reduced travel, saving on carbon gas emissions. They invested in a Zoom business license and continue to use the virtual platform to minimize their carbon footprint and save money.

In 2021, they remodeled and repaved the parking lot utilizing a combination of grey and green infrastructure, which helped mitigate flooding during large storms. What they have jokingly called “the DLZ lake” is completely gone now. They redesigned the parking area landscaping and implemented more green areas to the delight of their employees.

Last year, as a Columbus GreenSpot member, DLZ participated in Green Columbus. Their employees planted 80 Hackberry trees around the city, along with flowers, including butterfly milkweed, purple coneflower, black-eyed Susan, and partridge pea.

For Earth Day 2022, DLZ launched an employee contest to encourage employees to do their part by investing in the planet for a chance to win sustainable products. Additionally, DLZ will donate $15.50 per photo entry (up to $1,000) to carbon-offsets (the equivalent to 1 ton C02 emissions).

In conclusion, DLZ has demonstrated their commitment to protect the planet by providing a sustainable design and making “green” choices in everyday lives.

Gohio

Businesses across the country are talking about diversity, equity, and inclusion and adding these core values to their company’s mission. But are they considering an important component of equity called transportation equity? Does everyone in your company have the same opportunity to come to work if they don’t have the ability to drive or the means to own a car? Transit may be offered on the first shift but may not be available on the second and third shifts. Has your company addressed how to provide transportation equity on all shifts?

MORPC Gohio Commute staff can help provide you with the solutions to transportation equity for all employees and shifts. MORPC staff may even be able to help you with transportation funding to help start your transportation equity program. MORPC staff will consult with your company free of charge to help you tackle these important issues.

Gohio Commute is a program of MORPC. For more information contact Patty Olmsted, Senior Business Workforce Mobility Coordinator at polmsted@morpc.org

Plastic-free restaurants and food donation

Restaurants can play a big role in solving the plastic pollution crisis. Below are some tips on how to reduce or eliminate plastic waste:

  • Ditch the plastic straw and have metal straws on tap for purchase. Or go with paper or bamboo straws. These can be on hand in case a customer asks for a straw.
  • Buy in bulk. Those tiny condiment packets are plastic and they add up. Set up a bulk dispenser station instead.
  • Avoid plastic cutlery and stick with the real ones. Did you know that 100 million+ pieces of plastic utensils are used by Americans every day? Time to cut the plastic.
  • For takeout containers switch to compostable ones instead of Styrofoam.
  • Audit the purchases and determine if there is a plastic component that can be reduced or eliminated.
  • If possible skip the plastic wrap and use butcher, waxed, or parchment paper instead.

These are a few things that can be implemented at restaurants to reduce plastic consumption. On a similar note, if you have an excess of food don’t throw it away! Give it to furloughed employees or donate it to local hunger relief agencies. Check out Columbus Public Health’s Food Donation Guidelines for Licensed Food Facilities.   
For additional resources check out the Solid Waste Authority of Central Ohio’s (SWACO) From Waste to Resources flyer

Save More than Food campaign

Did you know that every day in Central Ohio nearly one million pounds of food enters the landfill? When food goes to waste, so does all the time, resources, and money that went into growing and distributing it. But together, we can make a difference. Save More Than Food offers the resources that you need to reduce your food waste at home, at school, at work, and in food businesses. Find ways to get involved wherever you. There are local resources, partner toolkit, and informational guides.

Learn how you can save money and protect the environment by reducing food waste at home, at work, at school, and in food businesses by visiting www.SaveMoreThanFood.org. Together, we can make a difference!

Are you looking to make energy efficiency improvements within an existing building before the end of the year? If so, consider the Innovative Energy Solutions Program from Columbia Gas. They provide rebates to customers to help offset the cost of making energy efficient upgrades that help your business save money and natural gas.

Here are a few examples of improvements that could qualify for valuable incentives:

  • Kitchen improvements, including the installation of ENERGY STAR® qualified products that use natural gas such as infrared fryers, steamers, pre-rinse spray valves and large vat fryers
  • Mechanical HVAC equipment replacements and system improvements, including condensing boilers, steam boilers, modular boilers, infrared heating systems, gas-fired steam absorption chillers, natural gas unit heaters and solar thermal pre-heat projects
  • Direct digital HVAC control and energy management system improvements
  • Air and duct leakage sealing
  • Insulation of attics, ceilings, walls, foundation areas, ducts, steam and water pipes, and industrial process piping
  • Domestic hot water heating system improvements
  • Process improvements

Get started today! Their team is ready to help you learn more about our program so you can take the first step toward saving. Simply email ColumbiaCommercialPrograms@clearesult.com, call 1-844-401-9731 or visit ColumbiaGasOhio.com/BusinessSavings to learn more.

Quick tip on lower costs and improving the environment

Paying invoices online reduces costs and improves the environmental footprint. Most simple accounting programs (ex. QuickBooks) give the option to pay invoices by clicking "Pay Now" in the email you receive, without having to print out a check, put it in an envelope, and slap a stamp on it. It may not sound like much, but if paying dozens or hundreds of bills a year, the cost and paper waste adds up. Additionally, offering an e-payment option to customers is another way to save time, money, and resources (and it is a GreenSpot commitment)!

GreenSpot does not require member organizations to re-up every year or ever to keep the GreenSpot designation. We provide a platform for them to track progress and offer ideas through social media and eNewsletters. We do strongly encourage annual reports from our members so we can calculate how much environmental benefit and cost savings our members have seen and to determine who is awarded the prestigious GreenSpotLight Award. Starting this year GreenSpot will begin contacting the business members one-on-one to see what type of successes and obstacles they are facing and will help them achieve their goals.

Big THANK YOU to you! We've surpassed the 20,000 member mark!! Our members have collectively have saved more than $13 million, reduced CO2 emissions by 41 million pounds, reduced water consumption by 145+ million gallons, and recycled 32 million pounds. Check out this video!

The Scotts Miracle-Gro Company, a GreenSpot member since 2019, recently released its 2020 Corporate Responsibility Report. The report outlines how the company continues delivering on its purpose––to GroMoreGood everywhere––both locally and across North America. It also announces the company’s environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategy for the next five years and provides an update on how the company responded during the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic to keep its associates safe and support communities while continuing to operate.

  • Engaging associates remotely during COVID on sustainability topics. The Marysville-based Green Team hosted a virtual “upcycled” mask-making class and authored many articles, including green work-from-home tips, advice on how to recycle correctly and confessions of a backyard composting novice.
  • Supporting 109 local garden and greenspace projects with monetary and product grants. These grants are providing thousands of Central Ohioans with fresh food and opportunities to connect with the natural world and their neighbors. Products donated totaled roughly 956,000 pounds of soils, mulches and amendments, or 18 semi-truck loads.
  • Promoting composting and recycling at the Marysville campus. In 2019, ScottsMiracle-Gro composted more than 20,000 pounds of food waste through its corporate cafes, supporting its company-wide achievement of recycling 5 billion pounds of green waste annually into new products.

GreenSpot does not require member organizations to re-up every year or ever to keep the GreenSpot designation. We provide a platform for them to track progress and offer ideas through social media and eNewsletters. We do strongly encourage annual reports from our members so we can calculate how much environmental benefit and cost savings our members have seen and to determine who is awarded the prestigious GreenSpotLight Award. Starting this year GreenSpot will begin contacting the business members one-on-one to see what type of successes and obstacles they are facing and will help them achieve their goals.

Did you know they are a GreenSpot?

White Castle

White Castle is proud to be a GreenSpot business member for over seven years. This membership continues the efficient and resilient legacy of their nearly-100-year-old company that survived the Great Depression and world wars through forward thinking, resilient business practices and conserving resources where needed.

Over the past few years they converted all their Columbus White Castle restaurant parking lot lights to LED, saving 4,500 kwh per month per Castle. They piloted a food scraps diversion program at their Home Office and within the Columbus Castles, diverting more than 1,000 pounds of food scraps monthly to a composting partner. They partnered with Smart Columbus and MORPC on a single occupancy vehicle reduction program. This partnership provided their local team members reduced-cost bus passes and a White Castle GOhio platform for ridesharing opportunities.

They are proud of their newly developed The Reach on Goodale mixed use campus, featuring their new LEED-certified Home Office building. Through an intentional and thoughtful planning process mindful of their internal Naturally Focused sustainability program, its construction incorporated many efficiency amenities, including:

  • Low-flow plumbing fixtures in the water closets, lavatories, breakroom sinks and showers;
  • Very efficient and long-lasting LED lighting throughout the building interior;
  • Energy-efficient heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) systems;
  • Real-time energy metering for energy efficiency and real-time utility data; and
  • Environmentally-friendly and healthy building materials and finishes such as carpet, ceiling tile, and paint. These are low emitting materials.
  • All reusable dishware and cups in the café.

These are only some of the great features of the new building. All their environmental sustainability efforts and programs help propel their long-term history into the future. White Castle remains a family-owned company that is dedicated to team members and customers while serving the environment and communities where they operate.

A Sustainability Manager plays a critical role within any organization. They help ensure that a business is committed to an agenda that will lead to a secure future, target and eliminate wasting resources, and help overall operations. Check out this video  that the City of Columbus, GreenSpot and three members put together to highlight those benefits. GreenSpot Matrix

Sometimes keeping track of the specifics of the commitments you pledged can be difficult. Each commitment has a different timeline, maybe different responsible party, and cost. To make it easier to do a deeper dive on the commitments, GreenSpot developed a GreenSpot Matrix spreadsheet where business members can track categories such as "responsible party," "cost," "payback period," "barriers to implementation," "timeline," and more. If your business is interested in receiving the GreenSpot Matrix document please email GreenSpot@columbus.gov.

Covid19 and sustainability

Covid19 has disrupted our way of life and the way business is conducted. Now more than ever, sustainability can help cut costs and get your company back on its feet. Did your company have to set up remote working in a hurry? If so, figure a way to keep it going. Does it make sense for employees to work from home (or other location) one day a week? Some benefits include reduction in greenhouse gas emissions from traveling, cost savings on business energy and water bills, less wear and tear on office supplies and equipment, improved staff morale (employee retention!) and productivity, and it may make you a leader in your field.

When disruption occurs it is easier for people to develop new habits. As your employees go back to the office, encourage them to take a green form of transportation. MORPC’s Gohio Commute provides tools employers and employees need to determine all the different options to get to work. The Gohio platform even calculates the cost savings, health benefits, and environmental benefits from each mode of transportation. Read more.

If you have to have in-person team meetings, consider holding them outdoors. Is your office near a city or metro park? If so, you could meet there for the meeting and work in a nature walk and/or bird identification. It’s a nice change of pace from office life.

item.title: Special Live-Stream Forum with Mayor Ginther
Help keep our parks and trails healthy and safe
item.description:
Residents Urged to Play Safe, Live Smart to Stay Healthy and Help Keep Columbus’ Parks and Trails Safe

Visiting Columbus Recreation and Park Department’s trails and parks are a great way to maintain your physical and mental health, but it’s important to Play Safe, Live Smart and take steps to use them safely.

Columbus’ trails and parks currently are open during the coronavirus (COVID-19) public health emergency. Our trails and parks are a resource to help residents enjoy the outdoors while engaging in recreation, exercise and education.

“In these times of great disruption, the health and safety of our residents is key. We have the ability to slow the spread of COVID-19 by rigorously practicing social distancing,” said Mayor Andrew J. Ginther. “Encouraging residents to use our trails and parks in a safe way helps prevent exposure and maintains access to these important resources.”

As the City of Columbus takes steps to protect residents and stop the spread of COVID-19, City leaders have carefully weighed the benefits and risks to public health of keeping facilities open.  At this time, the City is committed to keeping parks and trails open as long as it remains safe to do so.

While most residents are practicing social distancing at Columbus’ trails and parks, there are some areas where people are not doing as good of a job, including Antrim Park and the Olentangy Trail.

Play Safe, Life Smart: Practicing Social Distancing at Columbus Trails and Parks

Here are some tips to practice social distancing at Columbus' trails and parks:

Do visit parks and trails with your immediate family and those with whom you’re staying at home.

Do take advantage of opportunities to enjoy the outdoors for recreation, exercise and education.

Do pay attention to signage and barriers that restrict access to equipment, such as playgrounds, tennis courts, disc golf courses and basketball courts.

Do maintain a six-foot distance from others when walking, running and biking. You can do this by letting people know you are passing when you come up from behind and safely stepping off the path to let others pass.

Do NOT use parks or trails if you are exhibiting COVID-19 symptoms.

Do NOT step over or remove any barriers that block access to equipment, facilities and parking lots.

Do NOT play group sports using shared equipment, such as basketball, disc golf and tennis.

Do NOT use any equipment such as picnic tables, playgrounds, and basketball, disc golf and tennis courts. Currently, all recreation equipment is closed.

For additional information about COVID-19, visit Columbus Public Health, Ohio Department of Health or Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Additionally, Ohio residents with specific questions related to COVID-19 can also call 833-4-ASK-ODH (833-427-5634). For a full list of department-related updates and closures, visit ColumbusRecParks.com.

item.title: Columbus Public Health Steps-up Enforcement of Social Distancing and Hygiene for Businesses
item.description:
Beginning today, Columbus Public Health will step up inspections on businesses to assure they are complying with the Ohio Department of Health’s orders for social distancing and basic hygiene to slow the spread of COVID- 19.

“We are at a critical moment in slowing the spread of this highly infectious disease in our community,” said Mayor Andrew J. Ginther. “We have received hundreds of complaints that some businesses are not complying with the Ohio Department of Health’s orders, and we must assure that employees and residents are safe.”

Teams of sanitarians will visit businesses to assess the number of people working, if they are able to work at a safe distance from one another and if soap, water or hand sanitizer are readily available. Those not in compliance will receive a warning letter. A second violation will result in citations and could lead to criminal charges.

“We are pleased that most people and businesses are doing their part to slow the spread of COVID-19 by following the Ohio Department of Health’s orders,” said Dr. Mysheika Roberts, Health Commissioner for Columbus Public Health. “However, we continue to receive complaints from residents that some businesses are not following these orders. We will be sending our teams out to investigate these complaints in order to protect the health and safety of our community.”

Columbus Public Health will not be weighing in on whether a company or workers are essential, only if the place of employment is in compliance with the order. Guidelines for Essential Businesses can be found at corona.ohio.gov. 

“Businesses want to do the right thing, but may not know the full extent of the state’s social distancing and safe hygiene requirements. That’s why educating business owners and the public about how we slow the spread of COVID-19 is so important,” said City Attorney Zach Klein. “Our ‘education first, citation second’ approach allows people to learn about the state’s order while still giving health officials and law enforcement the ability to issue a citation if someone refuses to cooperate.”

item.title: Stay at Home
item.description:
Today, Governor DeWine issued a “Stay at Home” order which requires all Ohioans to stay at home, and limit trips to essential errands only. The order will go into effect Monday at 11:59 p.m.

It is important that we take this order seriously to stop community spread of COVID-19. We are at a critical point in our fight to stop the spread of this virus, and we must follow the governor’s order.

But this order should not cause panic, and I urge the residents of Columbus to act responsibly. You will still have access to the necessities you need to keep the community healthy and safe, including grocery stores, pharmacies and health care.

For government, businesses and nonprofit organizations that will remain open to serve critical needs and provide essential services, this is not business as usual. Employees who can work from home should, and steps should already be in place to allow employees to practice safe social distancing and assure proper sanitation. We should redouble our efforts to ensure steps we've taken to protect our employees are being followed in practice.

For individuals, to the extent you must leave home, follow the advice of public health experts. Limit your movement, practice safe social distancing, and wash your hands.

Finally, while these are challenging times, it is not a time for fear. Instead, we must rely on facts. Our decisions should put the common health and well-being of our community and our families first.

Be patient with one another. Support each other and be kind.

These are times unlike any most of us have ever seen, but together we will get through this and we will emerge stronger, smarter and healthier.
